messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity request — LumenData Q2 start

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. LumenData is ready to move from pilot to production and we need a dedicated pool for our forecasting workload starting mid-April. High level:
- Requirement: 12x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) dedicated for sustained throughput (24/7)
- Target start: 2026-04-15
- Expected steady-state Q2 token volume: ~1.2B tokens/month
- SLA expectations: 99.9% uptime, <120ms p50 generation latency for 1k-token prompts

Attached is a sizing spreadsheet (sizing_estimate_v2.xlsx) with their internal load curve and contract language they would like to mirror. Procurement is on standby — they want a signed dedicated commitment and an onboarding window no later than April 15 to hit their product launch.

One heads-up: SummitTech reached out to Redwood directly last week and their renewal for reserved capacity overlaps with the same GPU pool in our east-us cluster. We understand commitments matter — we just need to know if there is any path to secure this capacity before contract deadlines.

Can you advise next steps and whether Redwood can carve a dedicated slice for LumenData? We can be flexible on billing cadence if that helps.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Park
CTO, LumenData

SummitTech is on a multi-year commitment but their utilization has been ~55% historically; they do have an SLA-backed reservation. LumenData has higher ARR potential and procurement ready to sign if we can guarantee onboarding by 4/15.

Attachments: sizing_estimate_v2.xlsx, current_reserved_report.csv (attached)

- Operational impact: estimated engineering migration/downtime windows, rollout plan, and any SLA credit exposure.
- Commercial tradeoffs: what compensation/credit would be reasonable to offer SummitTech if we reassign capacity?

Thanks,
Sean
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:30:27 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — LumenData Q2 start

Quick assessment (high level):

1) Can we re-partition? Not safely without either:
   - Violating contract terms (if we remove reserved units from SummitTech) OR
   - Offering a like-for-like replacement (i.e., move SummitTech to equivalent reserved units elsewhere) which will take ~3–4 weeks of capacity rebalancing and testing.

2) Practical options (ranked):
   A) Offer LumenData a temporary carve-out from the burst pool (non-reserved, preemptible) with elevated price + a migration path to reserved capacity in 6–8 weeks. Pros: minimal SLA exposure. Cons: LumenData may reject if they need guaranteed capacity day-1.
   B) Negotiate with SummitTech to swap some of their reserved units for different region/hardware (we can offer credits). This requires SummitTech sign-off and ~3 weeks to move. Risk: SummitTech pushback and potential churn.
   C) Expand cluster by adding 8–12 GPUs on pre-provisioned hardware (spot purchase) — procurement lead time ~4–5 weeks; we could accelerate but cost will be higher for Q2.

3) SLA / credit exposure: If we reduce SummitTech's reserved capacity we will owe pro-rated credits and there is an escalation risk. I ran a quick financial check: offering SummitTech a 6-week credit + a 10% discount on next commit roughly neutralizes the churn risk vs the expected ARR from LumenData.

4) Proposed immediate recommendation:
   - Offer LumenData a guaranteed 20% carve-out (equivalent to ~3 GPUs) from burst capacity for an immediate start, plus an accelerated reserved onboarding that targets 4/15 via option (C) (hardware add + reimbursement mechanism).
   - Simultaneously open negotiations with SummitTech to rehome 4 GPUs to another region with a commercial credit; only proceed if SummitTech signs off within 5 business days.

I can put numbers into the one-page memo (cost delta, estimated credits, timeline). If you want a hard rec, I lean toward prioritizing LumenData given procurement readiness and strategic fit — but we need sales exec buy-in before committing to credits to SummitTech.

—Vivek
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

Subject: Allocation decision and next steps — LumenData dedicated capacity

Sarah / LumenData procurement — thank you for patience. After cross-functional review we are prepared to move forward with a solution that balances contractual obligations and LumenData’s launch needs. Summary of the decision and next steps:

Decision:
- Redwood will provide LumenData a guaranteed carve-out equivalent to 20% of the requested capacity immediately (3 GPUs from the burst pool) for onboarding and testing.
- We will prioritize the build-out of 9 additional GPUs to reach the 12-GPU target by 2026-04-15 using accelerated provisioning (hardware add + priority staging).
- To reduce SLA exposure for existing customers, we will offer SummitTech a commercial accommodation (pro-rated credit for 6 weeks + 10% off next reserved commit) in exchange for consenting to a temporary rehome of 4 GPUs to a staging cluster while we bring new capacity online.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- LumenData: sign and return the mutual action plan (DocuSign link below) — ETA 48 hours. (procurement@lumentech.io)
- Redwood Infra (Vivek): finalize provisioning plan and start ordering/allocating hardware — ETA 5 business days.
- Redwood Sales (Karthik): confirm billing cadence and finalize contract redlines with legal — ETA 3 business days.
- Redwood CS (Marissa): schedule onboarding runbook + canary testing window — ETA 1 week.

Commercial note: We will apply a one-time onboarding credit and offer a discounted reserved rate for the first 6 months as part of DL-9872. Final terms are in the attached contract_redlines.pdf.

DocuSign MAP: https://docusign.redwood.com/envelope/ABC-123-LUMEN
HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DL-9872

If SummitTech (ops@summittech.ai) has any objections, we will pause the rehome and execute the temporary carve-out + hardware add approach. We’ve CC’d SummitTech ops to be transparent and to give them the opportunity to respond within 48 hours.

Sarah — can you confirm procurement will return the signed MAP by EOD Friday? If so, we’ll begin ordering and keep you on a daily provisioning update until the full capacity is live.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
